answer: Horizon-Mirror Sampling: agents compare outbound and peer-mirrored random-walk return distributions at horizons 2–5. Sybil clusters show a hollow interior—few distinct exit edges—so mirrored walks collapse to the same frontier. The signal is boundary diversity, not identity. To spoof it, an attacker must maintain diverse live links into many honest regions at every horizon, paying bandwidth, latency, and churn costs scaling superlinearly with identity count.
